pr_title: fix(core): allow proper type inference when `ngFor` is used with a `trackBy` function
pr_body:
In #41995 the type of `TrackByFunction` was changed such that the
declaration of a `trackBy` function did not cause the item type to be
widened to the `trackBy`'s item type, which may be a supertype of the
iterated type. This has introduced situations where the template type
checker is now reporting errors for cases where a `trackBy` function is
no longer assignable to `TrackByFunction`.

This commit fixes the error by also including the item type `T` in
addition to the constrained type parameter `U`, allowing TypeScript to
infer an appropriate `T`.

Fixes #42609

comments: Could you please share a runnable reproduction. It could be related to #41995, but there can several factors as to why it behaves as it does. I cannot reproduce using a vanilla setup.

I'm getting this error as well in one of my components. Its cause is that in the template, the type of iterable is inferred as any[] instead of the actual type. Ex:

<ng-container *ngfor="let item of items; trackBy: trackBy">...</ng-container>

will fail, while:

<ng-container *ngfor="let item of castToProperType(items); trackBy: trackBy">...</ng-container>

will work fine. 

This happens in a complex template with nested *ngIf / *ngFor. I wasn't able to create a repro on StackBlitz yet, but I'll spend some more time on it.

Okay, I have actually [a small repro](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/JYOwLgpgTgZghgYwgAgCpUQawEIE8BiAriAmMAPYgA8qAfMgN4BQyyAFKACYQAeAXMhCEAtgCNoAGmTBIwgagCUAuCFwBuJgF8mTUJFiIUAOQgB3dFjxESZSjXrNWrKgFVkvSCE4BnNLQ5evAJCYpLSsgIuSsgq6lo6CAA2cN6+ALK4AMLJqYwsMVBQyqoA2gC6yAA+yMTcMKAQnBr5YBgIOAQgAdw8UjIQcsgAIlDkAA5D5KYgAJKy0d6toADmjMhQEGCEUCDIAOR7asja2kxJKb5Gy-jkUADyMDTIALwxqg75INe3DwCE8uUNKwvjcoBZ2nh-sgTOY2h1rKQKNQ6M1WIs4GQEMhSLcnq9Yv5QGNCGABAAFYDtKhXUEPexSPYgn4wPaVRnfMFwvB7WjRGnM+x5JzrTbbXZCRKJX5A45aZA6GDERGUZBgBCiNikfjIDLZC4KIXYyiLZCcYBQF7QjkPAB0OKgbAYgmtMAEWptcEKvykTM5llwbrAPBtrX9+F2mgUqNN5ptvoe8R0emg8CQw1GEyms1keLeuA+rBg5HI8g02iAA) now with the hint that the iterable should be `any[]`.

From my current understanding this is a legitimate error:

```
Type '(index: any, item: DropDownItem) => string' is not assignable to type '<U extends any>(index: number, item: U) => any'.
  Types of parameters 'item' and 'item' are incompatible.
    Type 'U' is not assignable to type 'DropDownItem'.
```

If the iterable is of type `any[]`, then a `TrackByFunction` that specifies its second argument to be a concrete type is unsound with the `any` it will be called with at runtime.

The change in #41995 means that the track by function's type has become contravariant, where it used to be covariant.

@JoostK 

I think in my case the cause has to do with *ngFor being embedded inside of *cdkVirtualFor.

Here are the relevant files:
https://github.com/mstawick/track-by-types/blob/master/src/app/app.component.ts
https://github.com/mstawick/track-by-types/blob/master/src/app/app.component.html

You can clone:
https://github.com/mstawick/track-by-types

and run `ng serve` and you'll see the error.

>This change breaks our previously working code (Angular 12.0.x in strict mode) like this:
>
>>error TS2322: Type '(_: number, item: Item) => number | undefined' is not assignable to type 'TrackByFunction<any>'.
>
>`<ng-container *ngFor="let item of items; last as isLast; trackBy: trackItemById">`
>
>`readonly trackItemById = (_: number, item: Item) => item.id;`

_Originally posted by @lucakohlgraf in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/40125#issuecomment-869530661_

It is not reasonable to get an error when your iterable is of type `Item[]` and your trackBy function looks like this: `trackByItemId = (index: number item: Item) => item.id`. Since you changed the Type of the second Argument of `TrackByFunction<T>` to `U extends T` it seems that TypeScript cannot infer the type anymore and `T` falls back to `any`. You basically _broke_ type inferrence.
Did you check the behavior in 12.2.0? The issue is still present
